paired.basis: paired sufficient-guidance hits over eligible answerable cases; exact McNemar two-sided p; percentile bootstrap of the hit-rate difference

notes.metric: sufficientGuidanceHit@3 requires every required facet to have an accepted citation in the returned three; scoreTarget owns the definition.
notes.recallInterval: macro recall and direct precision points are macro means; their Wilson intervals treat accepted/returned citations as the evidence units.
notes.clustering: case-level Wilson bounds are anti-conservative because the 120 answerable cases cluster into 10 family-level label signatures.
notes.unavailable: an output that is missing or errors is unavailable: it cannot satisfy abstention and counts against reliability.
notes.equivalenceRecall: an F04-style facet may accept two independently sufficient sibling sections; returning either one is a primary hit, but the unreturned sibling stays in the citation-level recall denominator.
notes.abstention: all no-match cases carry zero route hints and zero observed anchors, so abstention confirms support-policy wiring rather than near-miss discrimination.
notes.latency: p95LatencyMs is the per-case rerank time over the frozen candidate set in the offline scorer, matching the R3 measurement basis; it is not warm HTTP service latency.
notes.oneRun: this is the single pre-registered holdout run; no re-scoring or candidate change is authorized after this score exists.
notes.noTuning: no route, facet, packing, support, corpus, label, gate, or prompt was changed while producing this report.
